Rows of fenced plots along the river with open lanes between, a low workshop hut dug into the sand on each, smoke from casters' and smiths' hearths, boats drawn up on the bank and traders sleeping aboard them. No king's officer, no toll that anyone can name, no coin taken by count. In winter every hearth is lit; in summer a third of the men are away at other markets. What a skipper sees (Design/content/dossiers/ahus.md, section 1): - **What it is.** A permanent trading and craft town on the north bank of the lower Helge river (the "Holy River"), on sand: the archaeologists' Åhus II, or Transval. About 750 to 850 and a little later [C]. - **How big.** Over 12 hectares; about a hundred plots of about 25 m by 20 m, five to ten people each: 500 to 1,000 people, "several hundred" of them craftsmen. Far more than the district could use: they worked for the whole coast [C]. The game's size 2 is low for 793. - **Who rules.** Not known. Callmer says only that such a place lived under "the protection of local holders of power", that its people were mostly free, and that it could fight [C]. About 880-890 Wulfstan called "Sconey" subject to Denmark [W];. What stood there (section 2): - **The old market on the south bank (Åhus I)**, about 700 to 750, a few hundred metres upstream: three or four hectares, used for short spells, flimsy shelters only. Bead-making on a great scale (over 70,000 pieces of glass waste), bronze casting, comb-making, smithing; the finds match the oldest layers of Ribe. In 793 it is grazing land of Yngsjö village, 5 km upriver [C]. - **The clay cliff** in the river bank there: kaolin was dug for crucibles [C]. - **The town (Åhus II).** About 5,200 features dug. 149 sunken-floored huts (workshops and stores, not dwellings, in Callmer's view). Houses of the norse: one long room, earth floor, a hearth down the middle, smoke out through the roof, benches along the walls for sitting and sleeping. The chief's hall at Borg in Lofoten was 83 m long. (Design/content/peoples/norse.md). Faith of the place: old gods. Men from the woods bring skins and stand apart. An older Slav fort watches the river two kilometres below. You deal with whoever sits in the biggest house, and nobody takes a toll. What a skipper sees (Design/content/dossiers/aldeigjuborg.md, section 1): - **What.** A small craft and trading place forty years old, the only harbour for sea ships that cannot go up the Volkhov [Wde; WL]. Oldest timber 753 [Wen; Wru]. - **Name.** Northmen say Aldeigja (so the poem of about 1010); Aldeigjuborg, "Aldeigja fort", is the sagas' form [Wen] and fits only once there is a fort (870s on) [Wru]. description: The price leans up there. A small wedge pointing up. Goes with: With hud.tilt.down, its mirror. It stands after one of hud.word.*, which is 7 px high. At this size: Solid, gold. A mark is one or two colours on a clear ground, with no edge line round it: at 5 to 9 px the shape is the whole picture. Try it on dark purple (a window) and on night (the workspace bar). The look of the frame: dark plum with a raised edge, thick, with rounded corners. The light comes from the top left in every piece, so a raised edge is light on top and left and dark at the bottom and right, and a sunk one the other way. Gold marks what is yours to press or to spend. The letters are set by the game: never draw words into a piece. In the mock-up: Design/ui_mock/template3.html, layout G (Command frame). Size: 5 x 5 pixels. File to replace: hud/hud.tilt.up.png (same name, same size).

name: A window's title strip
where used: Along the top of each window, under its frame: the arrows, the name, the cross.
description: A window's title strip. A strip with a thin line under it. Cut in nine: the four corners, 4 x 4 px each, stay as you draw them. The top and bottom sides between them are 16 px long in the file and the game pulls them out to any length, so each column of a side must be the same as the one beside it: straight bands, no knot, no dither. The left and right sides, 2 px long in the file, are pulled out to any length, so each row of them must be the same as the next. The middle, 16 x 2 px, is one flat colour (clear in a hollow frame). Goes with: Along the inside of the top of hud.frame_window and hud.frame_popup: the same fill as theirs. From the left it holds hud.arrow_left, the panel's own icon (hud.panel.*), its name, hud.arrow_pick, hud.arrow_right, then hud.win_size, hud.win_open and hud.win_close at the right. At this size: 10 px high: the marks on it are 7 px. One thin line along its foot parts it from the window's body. The look of the frame: dark plum with a raised edge, thick, with rounded corners. The light comes from the top left in every piece, so a raised edge is light on top and left and dark at the bottom and right, and a sunk one the other way. Gold marks what is yours to press or to spend. The letters are set by the game: never draw words into a piece. In the mock-up: Design/ui_mock/template3.html, layout G (Command frame). Size: 24 x 10 pixels. File to replace: hud/hud.title.png (same name, same size).

name: Off the coast, by day
where used: The ship window, bottom right, behind your ship when she is off the coast by day.
description: Off the coast, by day. One low shore along the horizon on the left: dunes or marsh, no cliffs unless the port has them. A light swell. The horizon is 58 px from the top, the same in all twelve so they change without a jump. Keep the middle of the water empty: her own picture (ship_side, 160 x 96, the same size) is laid over this. Twelve views: four places at three hours. Draw the day view of a place first and make dusk and night from it by changing colours only, so the shore does not jump when the hour turns. Leave out boats, people and birds: her own picture is laid over the view. These views are a stand-in: the ship window is to become a live view of the ship in 3D (Design/DECISIONS.md, 7 October, ruling 11), so they are not among the pictures to draw first. The view is a small painting, not an icon: sky, water and shore in the game's 40 colours, hard pixels, no blur. In the mock-up: Design/ui_mock/template3.html, layout G (Command frame). Size: 160 x 96 pixels. File to replace: shipview/shipview.back.coast.day.png (same name, same size).

The placeholder is the tile the game shows now, made from real coasts (Bake/world/make_map_art.py from the world bake (level 2, 120 m), KK10 (1150 BP), ESA WorldCover 2021 and the scale-map bake's rivers and lakes). Colours now: forest = woodland; carr in the fen; meadow = cleared land: fields and pasture about 800; the salt marsh's ground; grass = heath and moor; the ground of peat and fen; grass with patches of forest and flecks of timber and reed light = peat bog, fen and marsh; meadow with patches of reed light = salt marsh; pale stone with patches of shallows = tidal flats; pale sand = beaches, bars and open dune sand; stone = bare rock and mountain; snow = snow and ice; shoal, one pixel = small rivers and streams. Keep the coast where it is: ports, sea lanes and fog are placed by real coordinates, not by the picture. Draw on a layer above it in the game's palette. The game reads tiles from Kapman2/MapArt/world: pull_art.py puts a redrawn tile into Art/final/map, and with --map also into MapArt/world (then run Bake\run.bat world\make_map_overview.py).
